skill.name: careers-to-jobs
skill.description: Reads public careers pages through Leadsets and returns a table of open jobs with source links. It checks scrape units and tests one company before processing the rest.
skill.summary: Turn public careers pages into a filterable table of open jobs.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The shell and reconnaissance flags are false positives, and the homepage and signup URLs are reference links. The workflow sends target domains or URLs to Leadsets as part of the requested scrape. Spreadsheet exports lack explicit safeguards for page text, and the batch steps do not specify how to enforce an approved spending cap before every call.

remediation.issue: Page-derived text may be interpreted as spreadsheet formulas.
remediation.suggestion: Write page-derived values as literal text in Google Sheets. Apply spreadsheet-safe text escaping to CSV fields before export.

remediation.issue: A batch may consume more scrape units than the user approved.
remediation.suggestion: Require an explicit unit cap before the first paid call. Check each call against a conservative cost bound and stop for approval if it cannot fit.

remediation.issue: Target lists are shared with the external scraping service.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose that Leadsets receives the selected domains or URLs. Send only the approved public targets and exclude unrelated spreadsheet columns.

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Page Text in Spreadsheet Exports
semantic_findings.description: The workflow preserves titles from public pages and exports them to CSV or Google Sheets. Without literal-text handling, spreadsheet software may interpret page text as formulas.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The export instructions have no explicit formula safeguard. Whether values are interpreted depends on the spreadsheet connector or CSV import behavior.

semantic_findings.title: Batch Quota Checks Do Not Enforce an Approved Cap
semantic_findings.description: The workflow checks remaining account units around batches, but a balance check does not enforce the user's run limit. A domain can cost multiple units.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The final checklist mentions user approval, but the run instructions do not specify a per-call cap check. No evidence was found of a connector-enforced cap.

content.user_title: Turn Careers Pages into Job Tables
content.value_statement: Comparing open jobs across company careers pages takes time. This skill gathers public postings into one filterable table and reports which pages could not be read.
actual_capabilities: Accepts company domains or careers URLs from chat, a CSV column, or a connected Google Sheet.
Checks available scrape units and tests one company before processing the rest.
Captures job titles, source links, and any team, location, or posting date shown on the page.
Filters jobs by keyword, team, location, or posting window and removes duplicate postings within each company.
Returns a chat table, CSV files, or Google Sheets tabs, with separate statuses for empty and unreadable pages.
limitations: Requires a paid Leadsets account with scrape units and a configured MCP connection or API access.
Cannot read pages behind a login, paywalled job boards, or pages that block automated access.
Leaves unstated teams, locations, and dates blank. It does not find contacts or verify email addresses.
Google Sheets output requires a separate connection with permission to write to the selected sheet.

use_cases.title: Review openings at selected employers
use_cases.description: See public openings at selected companies with locations and source links for follow-up.

use_cases.title: Track hiring across target accounts
use_cases.description: Compare recent sales and operations openings across an approved company list.

use_cases.title: Compare demand for specific roles
use_cases.description: Export a filtered list of public postings for a client report and document any gaps in coverage.

prompt_templates.title: List jobs for one company
prompt_templates.prompt: List the open jobs at [company domain] in a chat table. Include the title, team, location, posting date, and source link.

prompt_templates.title: Filter openings by role and date
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [company domains] for data analyst roles posted in the last 30 days. Report unreadable pages separately from pages with no open roles.
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare recent openings across several employers.

prompt_templates.title: Export postings to CSV
prompt_templates.prompt: Read the careers URLs in the [column name] column of [CSV file]. Check scrape units and test one URL first. Export US engineering roles and report gaps separately.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare job data for a separate analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Run a sheet-based review with a unit cap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use only the approved public domains in [sheet and column]. Test one domain and stop before exceeding [unit cap]. If you cannot enforce the cap, stop and report why. Write sales roles posted in the last 60 days and gap statuses to separate tabs. Treat page-derived values as literal text.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review a larger list with a spending limit and permission to write to the sheet.

output_examples.input: Show open roles at one company in chat.
output: Open roles: Northwind lists a Data Analyst role on the Analytics team in Portland.
The posting date is blank because the source did not provide it. The row includes the source link.

output_examples.input: Export recent sales roles for three companies.
output: Open roles: One posting met the sales and date filters.
Not found: One company's page showed no open roles. Another company's page could not be read.
Run summary: Four scrape units used.

best_practices: Share only approved public domains or careers URLs with Leadsets.
Set a scrape-unit cap and confirm the single-company test before processing a large list.
Keep source links and preserve the distinction between no open roles and a page that could not be read.
anti_patterns: Do not submit private links or unrelated spreadsheet columns.
Do not assume a blank posting date means a job is recent.
Do not treat unreadable pages as evidence that a company is not hiring.

faq.question: What can I provide as input?
faq.answer: Provide public company domains or careers URLs in chat, a CSV column, or an accessible Google Sheet column.

faq.question: Can I use the Leadsets free plan?
faq.answer: No. Job scraping requires a paid Leadsets plan with available scrape units.

faq.question: What gets sent to Leadsets?
faq.answer: The scraping calls send the selected domains or careers URLs to Leadsets so it can read the public pages.

faq.question: Does the skill estimate missing posting dates?
faq.answer: No. Missing dates, teams, and locations stay blank.

faq.question: How are unreadable pages shown?
faq.answer: The Not found section records unreadable pages separately from companies where no open roles were found.

faq.question: Can the skill find hiring managers or verify emails?
faq.answer: No. It returns job postings, not contacts or email verification results.
